newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares drop on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares drop on profit-taking.

text.p: Jordan's stock exchange fell on Monday in profit-taking which cut short a rally sparked by the passage of laws to overhaul the stock market and modernise company legislation.

The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped 0.11 percent to 151.84 points. More than half of Monday's turnover of 664,596 dinars ($938,694) was in two large bloc sales in Jordan Phosphate Mines and Jordan Ceramic Factories.
While Jordan Phosphates rose 0.02 dinars to close at 3.17 dinars, Jordan Ceramic lost 0.10 dinars to 7.10 dinars in trade worth 242,853 dinars and 186,375 dinars respectively.
Overall, falling shares outnumbered gainers by 19 to 12, with another nine trading but closing unchanged.
Brokers said the selling pressure which surfaced again may reflect a lack of confidence in the durability of a bourse rally after months of poor performance which has kept investors on the sidelines.
Floor traders could not resist the temptation to take some profits despite the burst of optimism on Sunday over the overdue passage of the reforms, they said.
But investment analysts are still hopeful the new companies and securities laws will jumpstart the stagnant market over the coming short to meduim term period.
They see an immediate knockon impact of the laws which reform Amman bourse operations and cancel a 15 percent tax on companies raising capital by transferring capital from reserves.
Arab Bank, which had promised to issue bonus shares once the reforms were passed, rose just 0.25 dinars to 256.25 dinars in only two transactions.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.15 percent to 79.34 points, still 4.86 percent down from the start of the year.
